smoke.verdict: NOT_RUN (no executable entry point — docs-only research mooring)
smoke.notes: The repo is offline HTML snapshots of the Moth Quantum API docs (intro, endpoints, 7 engine pages), the vendored MicroMoth source, and the vendored quantum-audio package. No runner exists to smoke. Cheap offline verification performed instead: text extraction over the exhibits confirms the contracts the labs consume (coin-toss-v1 v1.0.15 @ 2 credits/run; qpixl-v1 @ 1 credit encodes float arrays via Interwoven QPIXL; graph-v1 @ 5 credits prepares graph states; base URL + bearer auth + /openapi.json, 56 operations; quickstart submit->poll->fetch loop).

essence: Vendored quantum API docs + offline twins: the sourcing discipline behind lab entropy.

ideas.name: Know the source before you drink
ideas.statement: The primary sources for what quantum entropy CAN be are vendored verbatim: every public engine with its cost, version and schemas, plus the endpoint contract — a lab may not wire an engine it has not read.

ideas.name: Entropy has shapes; match shape to use
ideas.statement: The docs distinguish payload shapes — coin-toss aggregates, graph-v1 counts keyed by distinct 8-bit outcome strings, qpixl decode-noise floats — and jobs run submit->poll->fetch; the labs' probe-first selection policy is a direct reading of this menu.

ideas.name: Develop offline, deploy honestly
ideas.statement: Vendored twins (MicroMoth statevector simulator, quantum-audio schemes) give no-key local quantum semantics to build against; the self-contained per-engine HTML exhibits are the interface engineers actually read.

ideas.name: The menu feeds three labs
ideas.statement: This discipline is consumed, not admired: quilt-quant's moth_client, quilt-dba's mothqrc/vault, and MicroMoth's quantum-wow real mode each wire the documented engines with labels, caps and provenance — the research mooring drives the substrate for real.

parts.name: Vendored primary-source snapshot
parts.essence: The Moth Quantum docs are mirrored offline as self-contained HTML (intro, endpoints, engines): the stable, no-network ground truth about what quantum randomness and waveform services exist.
outputs: offline exhibits readable without a key
parts.failure_mode: Link-rot or paywalled docs would leave the labs guessing at engine semantics

parts.name: Engine menu with economics
parts.essence: Per-engine pages carry the decision fields: coin-toss-v1 v1.0.15 at 2 credits/run, qpixl-v1 at 1 credit, graph-v1 at 5 credits, labyrinth and entanglement-shader — version, publisher, updated-date, usage per run.
parts.gate: An engine without version + usage metadata is not selectable
parts.failure_mode: Choosing by name alone ignores cost and behavioral version drift

parts.name: Endpoint contract
parts.essence: Base URL https://api.mothquantum.com/api/v1, bearer auth on every call, machine-readable /openapi.json, 56 operations, identity via GET /me — the stable plumbing every client copies.
outputs: uniform request/response envelope for all engines
parts.gate: Bearer auth required on every call — no anonymous paths
parts.failure_mode: Quilt-dba receipted the .dev/.ai host confusion; the contract page is what arbitrates

parts.name: Payload-shape taxonomy
parts.essence: The engines differ in what randomness they yield: coin-toss returns per-job H/T aggregates; graph-v1 returns counts keyed by measured 8-bit outcome strings (each distinct key is a real sample); qpixl returns decode-noise floats — three shapes for three uses (stats, bits, entropy floats).
outputs: shape -> use-case mapping consumed by quilt-dba E-D3
parts.gate: A payload with no extractable per-bit variability contributes provenance, never fake bits
parts.failure_mode: Misreading shapes would harvest aggregates as if they were per-shot bits

parts.name: Async job lifecycle
parts.essence: Submit a job (POST /engines/{id}/process), poll status, fetch result — the quickstart loop every fleet client re-implements (moth_client, mothqrc, quantum-wow real mode).
parts.failure_mode: Fire-and-forget calls would lose job_id provenance

parts.name: Probe-first selection policy
parts.essence: The discipline the docs enable: probe with 1 tiny job, inspect result shapes, THEN choose the engine that yields genuine per-bit variability; hard caps on jobs (10) and target stream size (4096 bits) are set before any harvest.
outputs: a justified engine choice with caps
parts.gate: No harvest before a probe and written caps — the decision precedes the spend
parts.failure_mode: Harvesting blind would waste credits on engines whose shape cannot serve the use

parts.name: Offline twin strategy
parts.essence: The repo vendors the offline twins the labs develop against: MicroMoth (stdlib statevector simulator, seedable) and quantum-audio (QPAM/SQPAM/QSM schemes mapping audio onto circuits) — quantum semantics available with no key and no network.
parts.gate: Twins are labeled as twins — simulated semantics never claim hardware provenance
parts.failure_mode: Confusing twin output with hardware output would fake quantum results

parts.name: Exhibit interface
parts.essence: Each engine page is a self-contained HTML exhibit with request/response schemas, try-it links, and example outputs — the artifact format that makes the menu legible to a zero-shot reader or agent.
parts.failure_mode: A prose summary alone would lose the exact schemas clients copy

parts.name: Consumer lattice
parts.essence: Three labs wire this menu: quilt-quant (coin-toss probe, qpixl waveform round-trip -> entropy pool, graph-v1 tomography -> veto), quilt-dba (vault over cached packets; E-D3 live QRC stream), MicroMoth-quilt (quantum-wow real mode via comet-qrng-v1 with honest degrade).
outputs: applied entropy in trading, development and web randomness
parts.failure_mode: A lab bypassing the documented contract would fork the wire semantics

parts.name: Provenance chain discipline
parts.essence: The docs' job_id/backend/timestamp fields are what make downstream receipts possible: every fetched batch lands in caches WITH provenance (job_id, engine, backend, timestamps) and WITHOUT key material; labels live:true/mock:false only for completed real jobs.
parts.gate: No key material may ever enter a cache or receipt; provenance fields are mandatory
parts.failure_mode: Dropping job_id would make a randomness claim unreplayable and unauditable

cells.expr: offline HTML mirrors: intro, endpoints, 7 engine pages
submit -> poll -> fetch with job_id capture
1 tiny probe + written caps (10 jobs, 4096 bits) before harvest
quilt-quant + quilt-dba + MicroMoth-quilt wire the menu
caches carry job_id/engine/backend/timestamps, zero key material

layer_logic.0: Substrate: verbatim offline snapshots of the quantum API docs plus vendored offline twins — a no-network ground truth for what quantum entropy services exist and cost.
layer_logic.1: Mechanisms: the endpoint contract, the async job lifecycle, and a payload-shape taxonomy (aggregates vs per-bit keys vs floats) that turns marketing pages into engineering decisions.
layer_logic.2: Policy: probe-first engine selection with written caps before any spend, twins clearly labeled as twins, and shapes that may contribute provenance but never fake bits.
layer_logic.3: Interfaces: self-contained per-engine HTML exhibits, and the consumer lattice of three labs that copy this contract into moth clients, vaults and web plugins.
layer_logic.4: Evidence: the docs' own job_id/backend/timestamp fields become the downstream provenance seals — caches carry provenance and never key material, labels never lie about live vs mock.
